newsitem.title: USA: ATHome in Internet services deal with Teleport.
newsitem.headline: ATHome in Internet services deal with Teleport.

text.p: AtHome Network executives said they will on Monday announce a network serviced deal which will greatly accelerate its commercial services expansion.
Under the terms of the deal, Teleport Communications Group Inc. will provide AtHome with facilities management and network services for AtHome's AtWork business customers.

Both AtHome and AtWork incorporate the encircled a symbol, common in electronic mail addresses, as the first character of their names. In this story, the word "at" is used to represent the encircled a symbol.

Don Hutchison, who recently joined AtHome as senior vice president and general management of the AtWork division, said in an interview ahead of Monday's announcement that Teleport will greatly speed the availability of a variety of high speed, high bandwidth products for AtWork customers.
"This gets me nationwide in a heartbeat," Hutchison said.
AtWork services should now be available in the major metropolitan areas of New York, Los Angeles, Boston and Washington, D.C. by the end of June, he said.
Overall, the relationship is expected to speed the deployment of AtWork services in more than 57 major metropolitan centers, including Northern California.

AtWork will also be able to access business customers over broadband, high quality wireless links in 160 markets that are accessible by Teleport through its agreement with BizTel, a 38-gigahertz microwave services provider.
AtHome was formed in 1995 with financing from a combination of cable operators and the venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers.

The company distributes high-speed interactive services to homes and businesses using hybrid-fiber coaxial links and its own Internet backbone, or core network, which it can tune for optimal performance.
The AtWork division utilizes the company's own Internet infrastructure in addition to digital, fiber and cable-based connections.

But utilizing this high-performance system, managed independently and paralleling the Internet, AtHome aims to avoid performance degradation that has been evident with overloading of the public Internet. At Home's independent system includes nearly 7,000 miles of fiber optic lines.
The group can connect business customers' networks to the Internet, and link traveling or telecommuting workers back into the company network remotely.
Currently its products are available in metropolitan areas dotted across the United States.
Investors in AtHome include Tele-Communications Inc., Comcast Corp. Cox Communications and Kleiner Perkins. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
